business_object_format_rules.overview: This file defines the EXACT format requirements for BAW business object JSON files and their references in config.json. These formats are MANDATORY and non-negotiable for successful packaging and deployment.

requirement.title: Business Object JSON Structure
requirement.description: Business object JSON files MUST use the "type" field as the identifier, NOT a "name" field. The structure is strictly defined and cannot vary.

field_definitions.field: The business object type name (must match the name used in config.json)
Human-readable description of the business object's purpose
Array of property definitions (can be empty array if no properties)

property_structure.field: Data type: String, Integer, Decimal, Boolean, Date, or another business object type
Boolean indicating if property is mandatory

requirement.title: config.json businessObjects Array Format
requirement.description: The businessObjects array in config.json MUST contain objects with "name" and "file" properties, NOT string values.

field_definitions.field: The business object type name (must match "type" in the JSON file)
The filename of the business object JSON file (relative to widget/directory)

example.name: simple_business_object
example.description: Basic business object with string and integer properties

example.name: complex_business_object
example.description: Business object with multiple data types including Date and Decimal

example.name: multiple_business_objects
example.description: Widget with multiple business object references

example.name: wrong_business_object_structure
example.why_wrong: BAW's packaging system expects "type" as the identifier field, not "name". The "type": "businessObject" field is not part of the schema.

example.name: wrong_config_reference
example.description: WRONG: Using string array instead of object array
example.wrong_format: "businessObjects": ["UserData", "FormData"] ❌ WRONG: Must be array of objects
example.why_wrong: The packaging system requires objects with "name" and "file" properties to properly locate and include the business object files.

example.name: missing_required_fields
example.description: WRONG: Missing required fields in property definition
example.why_wrong: All four fields (name, type, required, description) are mandatory for each property.

validation_checklist.check: Business object JSON uses "type" field, NOT "name" field
config.json businessObjects is array of objects with {name, file}, NOT string array
Business object "type" value matches "name" in config.json reference
All properties have name, type, required, and description fields
Property types are valid BAW types (String, Integer, Decimal, Boolean, Date)
File names match the pattern BusinessObjectName.json

step.details: Use "type" field with business object name Include "description" field Define "properties" array with complete property definitions
step.validation: Verify structure matches mandatory format exactly Check all required fields are present

step.details: Add object to businessObjects array Include both "name" and "file" properties Ensure "name" matches "type" from JSON file
step.validation: Verify businessObjects is array of objects, not strings Check name/file correspondence

step.details: Confirm business object type name is consistent across files Verify file exists at specified path Check bindingType in config.json references correct business object

reference_widgets.widget: Excellent example of correct business object format - SatisfactionData.json uses "type" field correctly - config.json references it properly with {name, file} object
Corrected example after initial format errors - InteractionFormData.json fixed to use "type" instead of "name" - config.json fixed to use object array instead of string array

error_prevention.rule: ALWAYS read an existing business object file from a working widget before creating a new one to ensure format consistency
NEVER assume the format - always verify against working examples in the repository (SatisfactionData.json, TimelineData.json, etc.)
When creating config.json, ALWAYS use the object array format for businessObjects, never a string array
After creating business object files, ALWAYS validate the structure against the mandatory format before proceeding
